column1: # PB-BIND-3 traceability: every element the v1 screens need -> the facade method(s)
# that serve it. Enforced by coverage_test.go, BIDIRECTIONALLY:
#   - an element in the required list with no row, or a row with an empty method column,
#     is a COVERAGE FAILURE (the requirement's own words);
#   - an exported facade entry point that appears in NO row is an UNTRACED surface --
#     API the Android app can call that no screen asked for, which is how a bound
#     surface grows secrets and dead verbs.
# Method spec: "Type.Method" for methods, bare "Name" for package-level functions.
# THREE ELEMENTS HAVE NO DEVICE-REACHABLE WIRE VERB TODAY. They are listed, with the
# gap named, rather than quietly dropped -- PB-BIND-3 exists to make exactly this
# visible, and the requirement's own precedent (PB-PUSH-8, split across S8/S12 in 11)
# is that S8 owns the SURFACE and another slice owns the wired verb.

column4: note

DecodeQR is separate from BeginPairing so the scanner screen can DISPLAY the destination before anything is joined (PB-PAIR-6: no destination is joined silently). Origin is what the confirm sheet renders.
Returns the six-emoji SAS as ONE display string computed by the shared Go core (internal/remote/crypto/sas.go). The emoji table is never re-implemented in Kotlin.
State exposes the persisted pairing state machine's terminal states (declined, sas_mismatch, rendezvous_timeout, expired, already_paired).
Abandoned device keys and partial local records are cleaned up.
gomobile has no list type: a collection crosses as an opaque handle with Count/At. This is why Snapshot carries Text, not the []string of 4.1.
Group is VERBATIM from the wire (phonecore.CachedSession) and never derived on-device. status.Group is unbindable, so it crosses as its string form.
Machine presence via the relay (relay.Client.Presence).
Also serves the machine pane's activity log.
Delivery is via the EventListener; unsubscribe exists so a backgrounded screen stops the stream.
Renders daemon-sanitized SnapText only. No VT emulator on device (ADR-007 D2).
First-class verb (protocol/schema/remote.go ActionTerminalWatch, routed at remotegw/command_loop.go). The live tail depends on it.
Without unwatch the peek plane leaks per-session server render work.
Signed take_control; the burned seq gap (PB-STATE-8) is absorbed by THIS command frame, never by an input frame.
take_control_end.

Live-only: never queued, never replayed (ADR-007 D7). Paste is PB-INPUT-6's atomic entry for a clipboard paste or an IME COMMIT -- one event, not a keystroke stream, so it skips the 125 ms coalescing window and splits only at the 4 KiB cap; an IME PREEDIT deliberately has no entry point. UndeliveredInputs is PB-INPUT-1's "and that the UX state appears": input is live-only, so nothing here is ever retried, and the ledger exists so the user is TOLD what did not reach the machine instead of believing they typed it.

The LaunchSpec's ContentHash MUST come from the canonical protocol.LaunchContentHash. Reimplementing its length-prefixed encoding in the facade is FORBIDDEN (S1 review R2): a one-byte divergence yields silent signature failures with no compile error. See conformance/launch_hash KAT.

GAP: no wire verb exists. protocol/schema/remote.go defines launch/kill/delete/approve/device_revoke/take_control/terminal_watch/terminal_unwatch -- there is NO interrupt action, and remotegw opForAction maps only kill/delete/launch. S8 owns this surface; the verb is a cross-slice split in the shape of PB-PUSH-8.
Persistent Stop maps here (with confirmation).

GAP: ActionDeviceRevoke IS in the signed action set and the daemon serves it through requireRemoteAuthz, but remotegw opForAction does not map it, so a phone-sealed device_revoke is refused "unsupported command action" AND no reply is sealed, which would leave the phone's panic action looking like a success that hangs forever. So the surface seals nothing and records a durable refusal, exactly as interrupt does. Gateway-side mapping is owed.

READ ONLY, DELIBERATELY. remote_set_control is OWNER-TIER ONLY (protocol/server.go handleRemoteSetControl refuses the remote tier before the backend is consulted: "a remote device must never re-enable a switch its owner turned off"). The phone surfaces the state so a CodeKillSwitch refusal is legible; it must never be able to set it. The phone-side panic action is revoke.
Deletion on revoke/disable is part of the token lifecycle.

Two coarse toggles. Split recorded in 11: S8 owns the SURFACE, S12 owns the wired-to-real-verb test, because local filtering is insufficient (the push would still be sent and the provider would still see token/timing/size).

offline / connecting / online / reconnecting, plus two states that are NOT transport conditions and must not be rendered as one (S14): reauth_required means the Keystore refused the relay-auth signature for want of a fresh authentication -- the screen must offer a biometric prompt, not a spinner -- and repair_required means the key is destroyed, which is TERMINAL: the loop has stopped and the only recovery is pairing the device again.
PER STREAM, not global: a stale view is never presented as live.
Per-stream, rate-bounded per 6.0.
Idempotent.
Idempotent. Close releases the durable state handle for good.

NewApp resumes every durable coordinate (phonecore.Resume) and REQUIRES a KeyCustody: the state directory it opens is sealed per PB-KEY-2 tier under the Android Keystore, and there is no constructor that omits it (ADR-007 B18(c) -- cleartext must not be reachable by forgetting an argument). StateSummary is how a test -- and the debug screen -- observes that a restart actually restored, rather than silently starting from zero.

KEYED BY OPERATION ID. The unkeyed phonecore ReplyCache.Take is a recorded S7 residual: rebuilt from an unpruned OpOutcomes map, it can hand the app a stale outcome. The facade must route through TakeFor.

The ONE deliberate secret crossing (ADR-007 B8): a transient per-tier data key, unwrapped by an authenticated-Keystore AES KEK on the Java side and passed Java -> Go, zeroized after use. Inbound only. PurgeKeys is PB-KEY-7's lock purge. The AT-REST half of the same custody rides the reverse-bound KeyCustody interface NewApp takes (see lifecycle.restore); it is not an entry point, so it has no row of its own.
Events arrive on a Go goroutine; the UI must marshal. Queue bound and overflow behaviour are stated in the package doc and pinned by contract_test.go.
